sections.history: Naimisharanya, in Sitapur district of Uttar Pradesh, is one of the 108 Divya Desams and belongs to Vada Nadu, the northern country. Thirumangai Alvar sang it in a decad of ten pasurams, Periya Thirumozhi 1.6, honouring the lord Devarajan and his consort Harilakshmi on the banks of the Gomti, which the Alvar calls the Gomudhi. The decad is remembered for his mood of remorse and surrender. The temple here, the Shri Naimishnath Vishnu Temple, is counted among the eight Swayam Vyakta kshetras, the places where Vishnu is held to have manifested of his own will. In the Sri Vaishnava tradition the forest itself is worshipped as the Lord.
sections.architecture: More than any single building, Naimisharanya is a sacred landscape. The shrine of Naimishnath, or Devaraja Perumal, sits within the pilgrimage area, with the Goddess worshipped as Harilakshmi, also named Pundarikavalli. Its most revered feature is the Chakra Tirtha or Chakra Kund, a circular tank fed by an underground source, held to mark where Vishnu's Sudarshana chakra touched the earth. Pilgrims bathe here on festival days, and the Gomti flows nearby.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that the sages led by Shaunaka gathered in this forest and listened to the bard Suta recite the Puranas and the Mahabharata. The name Naimisha is explained by another tradition, in which the wheel, the nemi, sent by Brahma wore away here, marking the place as a hallowed ground. The circular Chakra Tirtha is revered as the spot touched by Vishnu's Sudarshana chakra, which is why a dip in its waters is counted so meritorious.
sections.festivals: Bathing at the Chakra Tirtha on the new-moon day falling on a Monday, Somavati Amavasya, draws pilgrims in large numbers, and in the month of Phalguna devotees undertake the parikrama of the sacred area. Vaikunta Ekadashi is observed by Vaishnava devotees. These observances are customary; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Naimisharanya asks the pilgrim to slow down: the temple, the Chakra Tirtha and the forest lanes together make one pilgrimage. Bathe at the tank as custom allows, offer respects to Devaraja Perumal, and read or recall Thirumangai Alvar's decad, which was sung here. Pilgrims often visit the other nearby sacred places of the kshetra, such as Suta Gaddi, along the way.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Naimisharanya lies in Sitapur district, Uttar Pradesh, on the Gomti, and is reached by road from Sitapur and from Lucknow, about 90 km away. Lucknow is the nearest major airport, and Sitapur and Lucknow are the nearest large rail centres.
